letter.subject: Concern about cookie and tracking activity following rejection of additional cookies on bbc.co.uk
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns about cookie and tracking activity observed on https://www.bbc.co.uk during an automated, passive audit carried out on 2026-11-08 00:17 UTC. Using a fresh browser, the audit detected the cookie banner, clicked “Reject additional cookies”, then visited https://www.bbc.co.uk/news, https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport and https://www.bbc.co.uk/weather, while recording what cookies were set and what requests were still sent.

The following points were observed:

1. Before any choice was made on the cookie banner, Chartbeat analytics cookies were already set: _cb, _cb_svref and _chartbeat2.

2. Before any choice was made on the cookie banner, Dotmetrics analytics cookies were already set: DotMetrics.DeviceKey and DotMetrics.UniqueUserIdentityCookie.

3. After “Reject additional cookies” was clicked, 30 requests were still sent to dotmetrics.net.

4. After rejection, 4 requests were still sent to scorecardresearch.com.

5. After rejection, 4 requests were still sent to chartbeat.com and chartbeat.net, and a new tracking cookie, _chartbeat4, was set.

6. After rejection, 2 requests were still sent to optimizely.com.

7. Your privacy policy at https://www.bbc.co.uk/usingthebbc/privacy-policy/ appears not to name four recipients that were observed during the audit: Chartbeat, Dotmetrics, Optimizely and comScore. I appreciate the policy may describe some recipients by category rather than by name.

In addition, our automated review suggests that analytics continued despite rejection, which appears difficult to reconcile with the statement in the policy: “We’ll only use them if you’ve agreed.”

Please would you:

1. Explain each of the points above.

2. Confirm which of these cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.

3. Stop any non-essential cookies or tracking that are set or continue to operate without consent.

4. Reply within one month.

If this matter cannot be resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker

ai_review.summary: The audit found analytics tracking before the visitor made a choice and continued tracking after the visitor rejected additional cookies. The principal additional concern is that the post-rejection activity conflicts directly with the BBC's stated promise to use functional and performance cookies only where the user has agreed. The privacy policy broadly addresses purposes, rights, retention and complaints, but does not identify the observed analytics providers by name.
